There is a slight difference between the statement and the written statement that was compiled together with Mr. McCloskey's team concerning certain facts such as meetings, because at the time before giving any evidence, in the statement I did my best to say that when it comes to meetings I really never participated in those meetings. However, in the statement of facts and plea agreement read that I did take part in two meetings and nothing more than that. That is what I wanted to clarify as regards my participation in these affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. I will put my question directly. In the original statement of facts, you referred to as -- it's related to forcible transfer again, and it's paragraph 1 of the statement of facts. You said: "During the attack and take-over of the Srebrenica enclave by VRS forces in July 1995, it was the intention of the VRS forces to cause the forcible removal of the entire Muslim population from Srebrenica to Muslim-held territory." And in your further statement, you qualify this as this: "The intention of the VRS forces to cause the forcible removal of the entire Muslim population from Srebrenica." You qualified this like this: "The first intention of the VRS was to physically separate two enclaves, the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica, to liberate the Zeleni Jadar, Jasenova, Milici road, and in phase 2 to reduce the Srebrenica enclave to the town area." And you said: "The forcible removal of that entire Muslim population from Srebrenica was the result of the fall of this enclave and subsequent decisions." So if you could elaborate on your statement which says the forcible removal was the result of the fall of the enclave and subsequent decisions, and how is it different from your first statement?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honours. According to what I know about what was happening about the fall and the capture of the enclave, I know precisely that the primary task was to separate, physically, these two enclaves, Zepa and Srebrenica. After the separation, and the separation was effected once the check-point in Zeleni Jadar was captured, which is in the southern part of the enclave, these two enclaves were separated and the road, Zeleni Jadar-Jasenova-Milici was rendered passable. The next task, as far as I know, was for the Srebrenica enclave to be reduced to the urban area or the town area. And of course, during the attack and during the operation, having seen that there was weak resistance instead of reducing it to the urban area, the whole enclave of Srebrenica was captured. What I know and what I believe, although I may be wrong, is that this was one part of the operation, so to speak a combat segment of the operation. Everything else that followed the capture of Srebrenica falls into the second stage of this operation which is the forcible transfer and departure of the population from Potocari to the Muslim-controlled territory. My intention was to describe precisely what took place, what was the primary goal, what was the next intention in combat segment of the operation, and of course what was the intention in the second stage of the operation. Of course, after the fall of Srebrenica a whole series of decisions were made, and there were meetings and agreements with the gentlemen from the international community, and finally a decision was made to forcibly relocate all the Muslims from Potocari; although, theoretically it was possible for them to remain there. But these were subsequent decisions, and they were not part of the combat operation. This is how I understand it. I only wanted to clarify this specific segment and to explain what actually happened. As for the attack on the enclave and the separation of the two enclaves started in June when UNPROFOR forces were moved from that road and when this road was freed. From the military point of view, that meant liberation of that area and making it accessible to become engaged in the combat around and over the enclave. This is how I understood it, and I tried to be as clear as possible. Whether I succeeded in that or not, I don't know. That was my intention. It was never my intention to dispute or deny that all the -- those who were in Potocari were forcibly removed from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it that you do not mean that at the phase 2, as you put it, the Muslim population were forcibly evacuated despite their wishes to stay in that area?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I really want to be quite clear. It was theoretically possible, and there were verbal declarations, in the sense that whoever wished to stay was allowed to stay, but now we come into the field of theory. As for practice, there was no possibility for them to remain there because there was so much hatred, there was so much blood spilled, and it made it impossible for anyone to stay there any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. In your further statement, you explained your role at Potocari as something of assistance or helping rather than coordination or command. While performing your duties, did you have the intention to forcibly remove this population yourself?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to say I absolutely made no decisions regarding this issue, and nobody asked me anything about it. If you want me to be candid, all those who are still -- who are living in Bratunac secretly wanted the enclave to be evacuated because of the situation that was prevailing there. I personally didn't suffer any casualties in my family, nor was any of my property destroyed or burnt. Therefore, I personally didn't feel any aversion towards those people, but nobody asked me anything or given me an opportunity to state my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before I ask Judge Prost or Judge Stole whether they have any, just a question for clarification purposes. You mentioned the second phase, namely when decision was taken to proceed with the taking over of Srebrenica, which ended up in the forcible transfer of the Muslim population thereof. Was this decision taken at the political level, political authorities level, or at military level or authority, or both, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no knowledge about how this decision was taken. I can only tell you what I think and what information reached me. The decision about what was to follow and how it was going to be effected was made by General Krstic until the arrival of General Mladic. Once General Mladic arrived in Bratunac -- or, rather, Srebrenica, and became involved in the combat operation, he was the sole decision-maker. Whether these decisions were in compliance and in accordance with the decision taken by the political leadership, I am sure that the politicians from Bratunac were in agreement for the Srebrenica enclave to be obliterated, but what the top political leadership thought, I really don't know. However, in the light of everything that I know, I think that that was the objective, and the decision by the top political echelons to eliminate or to annihilate Srebrenica as an enclave, that was their decision as well. Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. Judge Prost? Judge Stole? Okay. Mr. Nikolic, your testimony ends here. You've been with us for some time. I wish to thank you on behalf of the Trial Chamber for having accepted to come over and give testimony. On behalf of everyone, I wish you a safe journey back to where you came from. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Tansey. I thank you also for your presence here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's been a very silent role, but that's maybe a blessing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but silence is golden, as you know. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Nikolic can withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do documents. We've got several. Thank you. So, Prosecution. Mr. Thayer, you had, what, six documents you wish to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. And if I just may note one thing for the record. 65 ter number 4407, as we have noted here is the same as P02930, which is the joinder indictment to which another

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back in open session. Any objections to the admission of the Prosecution documents into evidence? We hear none, so these are all admitted. Popovic Defence team, you've got three documents. Any objections from anyone? The list has been circulated. No objections. They are admitted. Beara Defence team, you don't have any documents that you wish to tender, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. We think it's adequately covered in the record, so there's no need for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. The Nikolic Defence team, five documents. I don't see any difficulties here. No objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. These were the documents identified by the witness. And one more thing relating to the documents, we would like to say after the evidence given by this witness, our Defence team is considering to recall Witnesses Nebojsa Galic [as interpreted] and Jeremic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the interpreters heard correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- but we shall give it some additional thought and let you know in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Please do. Borovcanin Defence team, documents? You have three, six -- seven documents. Any objections? No objections. Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gosnell. Miletic Defence team, three documents, and two of which have not yet been translated. Any objections? No objections from anyone. Admitted. Last two will be MFI'd pending translation thereof, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: If I could just get any feedback from counsel on this P44 -- P4480, which is the report of the proofing session with Momir Nikolic, and you used it in the course of your cross-examination, Mr. Ostojic, but I take it from your position that you're satisfied what you read in was sufficient for your purposes and you don't wish to have it tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: And no other submission for it to be tendered by any -- any of the parties? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to make sure, Mr. Haynes, you don't have any -- you're not tendering any documents, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That concludes the Momir Nikolic chapter. Now, a few housekeeping matters and also some decisions, some oral decisions. Mr. Thayer or Mr. -- Mr. McCloskey has disappeared. Any news about tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm afraid we haven't been able to contact Mr. Parsons. He is in Amsterdam. As I understand it, he's making presentations at some kind of a conference or gathering and they go into late this evening, and we've not been able to get ahold of him, and I think he may be actually staying in Amsterdam, although I'm not sure about that. What -- the best solution I can suggest right now is if there's anyway to remain flexible, we can hopefully reach out to him, make contact sometime this evening. We may be in a position to start earlier tomorrow, perhaps not 0900 but -- but perhaps later in the morning or -- or midday, at least save a couple hours of evening time if he's available to start at that time. We just don't know, but we can keep trying to see if we can keep as much in the daylight as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The thing is that it's not a matter that is of interest only to us and to you and your colleagues on the opposite side. The trial -- the Tribunal needs proper --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understand we've got the security and all kinds of other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There's security, transport, and technical availability, et cetera. What I would like to know is up to what time does the Tribunal -- up to what time can the Tribunal wait before basically a decision is taken whether we are sitting in the morning or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Okay. We'll sit in the afternoon. Because we're -- as you can imagine on a day like tomorrow where we planned to sit in the afternoon, we do exactly as we did this morning. We meet early at 9.00 in the morning and we sit together in my Chamber and discuss various issues like we are going to do now. I think it's too late in the day now to shift to the morning session because of logistic purposes, so we are sitting in the afternoon tomorrow. I don't think we can leave everyone in -- hanging like that, not knowing -- if instead you find a solution, but you have to have everyone, including -- then let us know, but I think it's too late in the day now. So we are adjourning till tomorrow afternoon, but before we do that, there are a few other matters. Let me just consult with my colleagues on something first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait. Wait a moment, because I don't like surprises at half past 5.00 in the afternoon. Mr. Registrar has just informed us that there is another witness waiting, Mr. Janc. I hope he has been told that Mr. Parsons is going to testify before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, we -- some of us are feeling like we were just inches from a clean getaway. We have actually made efforts to fill as much court time as possible. We've engaged in discussions with our friends. Mr. Janc is available to present his direct, I think, probably put on his direct testimony this afternoon in the balance of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We have agreed with what we believe is a reasonable request from our friends that his cross not begin until Friday after Mr. Parsons has begun and completed his testimony. And that's -- that's the agreement we reached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's -- and in fact, we thank you for trying to utilise the court time to the best possible. Now let's go into private session for a communication basically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We are in open session now. We are deciding orally two motions. The first one -- I'll give more details soon, but the first one is Popovic's motion to recall Professor Dunjic and Professor Stojkovic, and also Popovic motion for clarification of one of the decisions that we gave recently on the Prosecution's motion to admit evidence in rebuttal and to reopen its case. Now, to start with, we are advising the Prosecution that we do not require a response from you to the Popovic motion for clarification, which I just referred to, and we start from here. The Trial Chamber is seized of Accused Popovic's request to recall Professors Dunjic and Stojkovic. This motion was filed confidentially on the 8th of April of this year. And we are also seized of his supplemental request concerning the proposed testimony of Professor Dunjic, with an annex, and this was filed on the 22nd of April. In it, Popovic indicates Professor Dunjic's availability to testify. And then we are also seized of Popovic's request for clarification of the further decision -- a decision on the Prosecution's motion to admit evidence in rebuttal and to reopen its case. This motion was filed, as you are all aware, yesterday. Now, the Prosecution filed a confidential response on 21st April to the first of the motions I mentioned, stating that they do not object to Popovic's application to recall Professor Dunjic and Stojkovic, and that it would not object to the admission of their evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis without close cross-examination. Yesterday, Popovic filed a confidential reply agreeing to tender evidence from Dunjic and Stojkovic pursuant to Rule 92 bis. Since Professor Stojkovic is being called in relation to the testimony of Prosecution witness Parsons, Popovic requests permission to file the Stojkovic statement at least seven days after the testimony of Prosecution expert Parsons. Also, yesterday Accused Popovic filed a confidential notice concerning Stojkovic's availability to testify. We have deliberated on this, and considering that the Prosecution does not object to recalling Professor Dunjic and Stojkovic, and bearing in mind the relevant part of this Chamber's further decision on Prosecution motion to admit evidence in rebuttal and to reopen its case which we rendered on the 27th of March, we grant Popovic's leave to reply. We grant Popovic leave to file the proposed statements from Professor Dunjic and Professor Stojkovic to be considered for admission under Rule 92 bis, and allows Accused Popovic no later than seven days after the conclusion of the testimony of Parsons to file the Stojkovic statement. The Prosecution will have two days from the date of the filing of each statement to raise any objection to their admission pursuant to Rule 92 bis. Given that both statements will be filed for consideration for admission pursuant to Rule 92 bis, there is no need for the Trial Chamber to consider Popovic's supplemental motion or comment upon the notice at this stage. Accused Popovic further requests that the Trial Chamber instruct the Prosecution to obtain and disclose a sample of cases from ICMP which have not been selected by the latter. The Trial Chamber sees no merit to the argument made by Accused Popovic that the ICMP selecting the samples of new identifications affect the quality of the data. At the same time, the Trial Chamber reiterates its instruction that the Prosecution diligently pursue disclosure of samples with the ICMP and notes again that any inaccuracies or inconsistencies in the ICMP evidence will affect the weight to be attributed to it in light of the entire trial record and not its admissibility. Furthermore, the Trial Chamber holds that in light of this finding, the further decision on Prosecution motion to admit evidence in rebuttal and to reopen its case, which as I said earlier we rendered on the 27th of March, is sufficiently clear and requires no further clarification. For these reasons, we dismiss the second request made by Popovic and the request to recall Professor Dunjic and Professor Stojkovic and deny the request for clarification of the further decision on Prosecution motion to admit evidence in rebuttal and to reopen its case. That's it. So now we can call --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. All right. It's being suggested by my colleagues, and I willingly agree, that we take the break now. It will be of 25 minutes' duration. In the meantime, Professor Janc -- Investigator Janc, okay, will be informed that he will start testifying soon after. Half an hour break. Half an hour break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Janc, good evening to you and welcome. You are about to start giving evidence as a Prosecution witness pursuant to a decision that we have taken. Before you do so, you're familiar with the procedure, you need to make the solemn declaration. Please read it out aloud, and that will be your commitment with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you and good evening, Your Honours and colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Good evening to my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Good evening, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Would you state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: My name is Dusan Janc.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And are you currently employed with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What is your title?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: My title is investigator.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what are your duties and responsibilities as an investigator for the OTP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: As investigator for the OTP, my responsibilities are -- and duties are normal investigative activities such as obtaining and collecting evidence. For example, interviewing witnesses, victims, and suspects; reviewing, analysing documents; preparing and carrying out the missions. There are also activities related to the ongoing trial, then preparing the reports and witness statements. Yeah, this would be the activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: When did you begin your employment with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It was on the 1st of June, 2006. So it will be three years now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And could you very briefly describe for us your career in law enforcement up to your employment in the OTP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. I joined the Slovenian police in July 1993 when I finished my secondary police school in Ljubljana. First I was a regular police officer in police station Kranj for one year. Then in September 2000 -- in 1994 I became criminal investigator at the same police station, dealing mostly with minor criminal offences. In September 2000, I was promoted to criminal investigator at the police directorate within the same area, so -- and I was attached to the organised crime department. So from then on I was dealing with the organised crime mostly. Most of my cases were related to smuggling of elicit drugs. Between 2003 and 2004, that was between June 2003 and 2004, I was in Bosnia in European police mission, when I was advisor to the criminal investigation department of the Republika Srpska in Banja Luka. Then I returned back to Slovenian police, so to the same department, same office as before, dealing with organised crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And during the period of time you were serving in Republika Srpska, what were you duties?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: The mission, European police mission, was monitoring and advising mission, so we were -- we were advising and monitoring criminal investigation department within the Republika Srpska entity. So these were our -- our duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Janc, during your law enforcement experience in the past did you ever testify?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, several times so far. I cannot -- I don't know how many times so far, but several times as investigator.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, turning to the reason you're here today, what -- what is the reason you're here today?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. For this trial, I prepared the report regarding the exhumations and identifications of individuals which were -- which are related to the fall of Srebrenica. So I have prepared the report which is why I am about to testify today.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And I take it that this -- the document you're holding in front of you is your -- a copy of your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I have a copy of my report together with all the attachments which are part of the report itself. That's all I have here with me today.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Janc, what was the purpose of this report? What were the main objectives of this report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: There were several objectives of this report. First one was to present the most updated number of identified individuals related to the fall of Srebrenica or related to the -- or to present the number of the individuals which are coming out of the exhumed graves. The second objective was to present the surface remains which were collected during the -- this period in different areas within Bosnia and Herzegovina and are related again to the Srebrenica events. Within my report there, you will find also the section where I am talking about the DNA connections between the different graves. So that was the third objective to present to the Trial Chamber, what you can find in the different data regarding these connections. So -- and the last objective was also to present all the new exhumations which were done between Dean Manning 's testimony here and today, and these are also reflected in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. What were your main sources in preparing this report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Our main -- my main source was indeed the ICMP March 2009 update, which was provided to us at the beginning of March this year and includes the identified individuals as of 31st of January, 2009. Besides that, I also used -- yeah, I was also using different sources which I obtained from the BiH authorities mainly, so -- and these were documents provided to us by the Tuzla prosecutor and Tuzla court. Second portion would be BiH state court prosecutor, prosecution office; and the third would be BiH Commission on Missing Persons. Actually, no, it's BiH Institute on Missing Person. So these were main -- main sources where we obtained -- where I obtained the documentation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And have you personally visited or observed any of the grave-sites cited to in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. That was mission conducted in -- I think by the end of October 2007, when we visited all the primary and secondary mass graves together with the members of the BiH commission on missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, could we please have an e-court exhibit, 4490.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. This is my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And can you briefly lay out for the Trial Chamber what the basic layout is of your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, my report consists of first part which is actual report on four pages, and then we have four attachments in annexes. So Annex A is actual update of Dean Manning's report, and everything you can see there in red text, that's in addition to Dean Manning's report. Then Annex B is related to surface remains section where I explained the findings regarding the surface remains section. And then we have Annex C, which is related to the connections between the graves. There is -- there are many tables attached to this annex and also a chart. And the last one is Confidential Annex D where you can find individuals by name which are part of the total number which are currently identified in and are in fact my report. So here you have a list of all the individuals by name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And if we could briefly have on e-court Exhibit 4491, and if it could please not be broadcasted. If we could please go to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And can we look at the third page also, please. And the fourth. Thank you. Can you describe for us briefly what this is, what this document is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: As I explained before, this is part of the Confidential Annex D, and these are the individuals which were found and identified in Cerska grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you explain also to the Trial Chamber how Confidential Annex D is laid out?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Or what portions it consists of?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. Confidential Annex D has several parts. First part is related to the graves. So both three types of graves which I made up, mass graves, smaller graves, and individual graves. Then is a portion of the other and Serbia-related graves, which is followed by surface remains section, and the last part is -- just -- is, yes, there are individuals related to the DNA -- DNA connections.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And can you tell us what the difference is between the DNA connections presented at Annex C and DNA connections presented in your Confidential Annex D?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. What you can see now on the screen and also what is also part of the DNA connections portion of this confidential annex, these are the entries which are taken from the ICMP 2009 -- March 2009 update. You can see the exact entries as you can see them here in that -- in that list. So what is included in Annex C is, I would say, more investigative -- investigative work. So there you don't have names, but you have actual connections between the graves included.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And we will go -- we will go into that shortly, but before that and before I go into some questions about the methodology you used, I'd like to ask whether you received any assistance with the preparation of this report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. When we are here with these connections, I can say that I was assisted by our analyst Panayota Vassou, who was mainly dealing with the connections regarding my report, upon my supervision and upon my instructions, and she also provided the chart that is attached to the Confidential Annex C. Then also during the finalisation of the report I was assisted by yourself regarding grammar and language, because I'm not a native speaker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. When you say I was assisted by our analyst, could you repeat her name again and what do you mean by "our"? That means a member of the Office of the Prosecution or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes. I mean the member of the Prosecution, our team, her name is Panayota Vassou.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, what was the main source of information used for your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, as I already explained the main source was indeed the ICMP March 2009 update.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And for the record, the complete March ICMP update can be found as Exhibit 4494.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Did you use any other sources of information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. I also used the other sources, mainly exhumation records, some autopsy records, also photographs, but mainly I was focusing -- focusing on -- on exhumation records regarding the -- regarding the exhumations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could we please have on e-court Exhibit 4493, and not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you tell us what this page represents?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. This is sample page I prepared in order to present you the methodology I have used in order to get the numbers for the individuals. So this is --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What is it a sample page of?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: This is a sample page of the ICMP March 2009 update. When you open the file, you will get the results as you can see them here on the screen. They will appear on your screen as well. So these are only first 30 entries out of more than 10.000 entries which you can find on that -- on that spreadsheet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And the colours of the rows, for example, the greys and the pinks, are these yours?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No. This is -- this is everything what you can see on screen is done by the ICMP, and you can see it as it was provided to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: So different colours are, yeah, done by -- by there side. So I can explain these colours, what did they mean, what -- what kind of information we have about these colours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Grey colours are not that significant, so they're included all. Probably they are using this as a background. But we have different slight yellow colour here. So if you see the colour, the entries in this colour, that means that the relatives of this particular individual -- individual have not been informed about the result of the DNA match.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Can we go to the next page, please. Mr. Janc, can you tell us what the difference between this page and the first page is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if I may, I will explain first these different colours, because we can see here orange colours also or something, and I'll explain what this represents. So the colours -- the entries which are in this colour means that these are new entries in relation to the last -- to the previous update they have sended to us; in November, for example, was the previous one. ICMP sent us the updated list of the individuals, and if you find the individuals in these new March update in this colour, that means that in between these two dates these were added as new identifications. So -- and that I respond to your question, this is also, okay, sample page, but we are moving towards how -- how I came up with the numbers which are included in my report for each in particular grave-site. So what I was doing, you can see here that first step was that I sorted the -- the entries or sorted the data by case ID. This is first column on the left-hand side. And you can see they are going alphabetically. So I have taken example from the same March 2009 update and to present you how it looks like when you have, you know, sorted -- sorted version of the same data.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go to the next page, please. Can you describe what we see here, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. This is -- can we go more to the left? It's more -- no, left, please. Yes. This is more important. First column is more important. So this was next step what I was doing. In order to -- to find how many individuals we have in certain grave, I had to extract or I had to find particular entries related to these particular graves in this spreadsheet. So you can see here, for example, if you are looking into the first column, case ID is BIS 01 SEK. So that means this site is related to Bisina. So I have included this site because it appears the first -- the first mass grave if you sort it by alphabetical order. So I've used this Bisina site as an example. So what I was doing with the -- with the ICMP data was that when I sorted this data, I was copying each and every single entry which you can see in the previous sample into special spreadsheets. So -- and these special spreadsheets now relates to one and single particular grave as you can see it here now on the screen. So this is the result, what you get when you copy each and every single entry from that main spreadsheet into separate spreadsheets.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And is this the final step?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No. This is not the final step yet, and I can explain it why. If we can move to the right a little bit. You can -- and if you look into the last column where it says "Type Of Report," you have "Main Cases," and then you have "Reassociations." Currently on the screen we can see only one, but I think there are two more in this down there. So reassociation means that one individual -- or body parts of the same individual were found in different grave or different location all within the same grave, you know, in different grave or in different location. All within the same grave, you know, in different location. So it means that these cases are reassociated to the main case. So in order to get the exact number of the individuals which are coming out from particular grave, that you don't count any individual twice, you can take into consideration only main cases and that's what I was doing. So when I got this spreadsheet, then I filtered the last column which says "Type of Report" by main case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go to the next page, please. Can you tell us what you see here, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly what I was explaining before. So you can see again it is grave-site related to Bisina, and if we can move to the right again. So this is the final result when you have only main cases included. So -- and then you just count how many of them you have on -- on the list, on the spreadsheet, and that means that many individuals have been identified from particular grave-site.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we go to the last page of this exhibit, please, page 7. Now, Mr. Janc, can you explain to us what this is or what this represents?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: You can see these are again data from the same spreadsheet, ICMP update. So -- but these cases are related to the connections between the graves. So in order to get this kind of spreadsheet, so you would have to sort it, the spreadsheet, by "Protocol ID," which is the fourth column from the -- from the right. So you can see it on the top, "Protocol ID."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: If we could maybe close in on the very top five rows, please. So can you describe for us specifically --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: -- what you have there.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Protocol ID is important in order to find one individual. As I understand this data, one protocol ID can be attributed only to one individual. So -- and in case the body parts of one individual have been found in different graves, you will find these connections. As you can see it here, if the -- if you see the red entries -- so and just to clarify that, these are my colours, so I put it that you can follow it. So this red, blue, and then we have green, and at the bottom there are also, I think, brown ones. So these are five connections which you can find in that spreadsheet. So, for example, if you look into the first one, the red one, you can see from the case ID that this particular -- particular individual was found or his body parts were found in Budak number 1 grave, as well as Zeleni Jadar number 4 grave. Although you can see here Zeleni Jadar number 8, it is actual our number 4. So it is reflected in my report, because sometimes -- or very often now the BiH commission are putting their own markings. So in order to be consistent with our markings, I am calling it Zeleni Jadar number 4. So you have -- in order to get the connection between two graves, it is important, as I explained, that you have sorted by protocol ID, and then you have to consider the case ID.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And how about the next situation, the writing in blue? Can you briefly just comment on that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. It's the situation where we have two brothers, and we can say that one of those brothers have been identified in three graves. So why one? Because we have only -- the protocol ID is 7924, for example. That means for all three entries, that means that one of those two brothers have been identified. We just know -- we just don't know who of those two brothers. So -- and on the left-hand side you can see that body parts of this individual have been found in three different graves, Budak 1, Budak 2, and again Zeleni Jadar number 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: And if I just can add something. If you can move to the right again. More. Okay. To the end. Okay. Thank you. And as you can see it here, "Type of the Report." So in order to get a conclusion regarding the connections, you have to take into considerations -- into consideration both main cases as well as reassociations. So this is the difference between counting the individuals found in particular grave or of trying to find the connections between the graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Janc, can you just summarise what is the main identifier you look for when you are looking for connections between graves or for reassociations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: The main identifier is, as I explained before, is protocol ID.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And if, for example, we were to take the protocol number for -- right at the top of this example, protocol ID 7923-06, where could we find this example in your report? Can you show us?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. This can be found in Annex C.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could show us specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And for that if we could go back to Exhibit 4490, and it can be broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, I found it. It is in Annex C, so I can give you the ERN number. It is X0194280.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: That will be page 50 of the report. And can you tell us where we need to look, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. It is -- if you look into the first column. So you will find it the fifth entry from the top down. So you will see the number 7923/06, and this --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What is this number?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: This is protocol ID which you can see it in the previous spreadsheet. Next to it are our markings, to which particular site is this individual -- or where you can find the connections between the graves. So between Budak 1 and Zeleni Jadar 4, as I explained before. And on the right-hand side you will see the site codes which you can also find in the previous spreadsheets.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: So ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Janc, you had mentioned that Annex C of your report also contains a chart at the end.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we go to the last page of this exhibit, please, page 65. Can you briefly explain for the Trial Chamber the meaning of this chart.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. This chart was prepared, as I explained before, by our analyst, and it is DNA connection chart between disturbed mass graves. You can find all the connections between the graves which are listed in the table we have just seen also in this chart. So you will find how many different cases were found to be connected between different graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And when you say "cases," what to does it mean, a case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: A case, it means one connection. So if there is -- if there were body parts of one individual found in two different graves, that means one connection, one case. If body parts of one individual were found in three different graves, as we have already seen that example also, then there would be three cases. I would count them three times, for example, because you have connection between grave A and B, A and C, and B and C. So three times would that individual be counted -- not individual, but I would count three cases as three DNA connections.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And just briefly looking at the chart, can you just looking at it tell us what kind of DNA connections you see here between which primary and which secondary graves? Just generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Okay. We can see here from -- from this chart it is also -- part of the chart also shows the forensic evidence which were already known before between these graves which connect the primary and secondary graves, and also beside that on the right-hand side in -- in -- in red lines you can see the connections between -- between the primary and secondary graves, how many cases, how they are connected, and, yes, you can see between Branjevo farm and the -- the graves which are in Cancari Road, secondary graves in Cancari Road we have 20 cases, so 20 connections. Between Kozluk and Cancari Road we have 55 -- 52 of those connection and so on. You can -- it speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Do you also summarise this data anywhere in your report? The data regarding specific connections between graves.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, indeed. It is part of the Annex A. At the end of each -- each grave, you can find the explanation regarding how many connections we have between this particular grave with the -- the other graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And, Mr. Janc, are all the connections that you identified from the ICMP March update, are they all reflected in this chart?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you please explain why?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. In the ICMP update we have also find -- we have also found the connections which are not included here, and we -- I think the best way would be to look into the spreadsheet, and I can explain why.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. If we can go two pages before this one, so page 63 of this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the -- this is the table, what I was talking about. And first column you can see I've marked it as "Not counted." So it means if you see "not counted," that means they're not reflected in chart or in my report but I have put them here because think found them into -- into the spreadsheet, into the ICMP update. So -- and there were several reasons why I did not include these particular cases into -- into the total count.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please give us some concrete examples?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. Most of them are related to connections between Ravnice 1 and Ravnice 2, as you can see it at the end of or from the second part of this table, and also on the next -- next page you will see more connection between those two graves. So I did not include Ravnice 1 and Ravnice 2 because what I was including were disturbed graves. So we all know that Ravnice is not disturbed grave, and I did not include into my chart. Although I did not include them, it doesn't mean that they're not important. They are important and significant, because it shows that actually Ravnice is most probably one grave. So because we have so many connections, but it was just exhumed in two different -- in two different occasions. So we have -- that's for Ravnice. The second -- the second reason why I did not include some of them are those which are between Glogova itself. You can see them, for example, the second entry, Glogova 2 and Glogova 8, because we are counting -- we are considering Glogova -- Glogova 2, sorry, as -- as a grave with several sub-graves. So from -- going from 2 up to 9. And you have, as you can see here, several such connections between Glogova 5 and 7, 5 and 9, these connections. So I did not include those either.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: And the third reason or series of these cases were the ones which were, at least at the time when I was preparing the report, somehow illogical. And you can see, for example, which are those cases on this spreadsheet. I can -- I can tell you it's the first one --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Maybe it's easiest if you give us the protocol number?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: The protocol number 8019/06. Then --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And can you tell us why it's illogical?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Okay. This one. This particular one it's illogical because we have connection -- we can see connection here between Cerska and Hodzici. So we all know that Cerska is primary undisturbed grave and Hodzici is secondary grave. So it is not logical to me that there can be any connection. So then if we move to the case which is the third one down, protocol ID 2741/03, connection between Glogova 5 and Cancari 3. Glogova 1 -- Glogova 5 is actually primary grave, and Cancari 3 is again secondary grave, and so far we have no evidence that these two graves are connected -- connected. Then if we move down, we have a connection. It is protocol ID 157/02 between Hodzici 5 and Zeleni Jadar 5. Again, same reason. We don't have any indications that these two secondary mass graves are connected. Next one was 3122/03 between Kozluk 3, Cancari 3, and Liplje 2. So here we have the same problem because there were no established problems so far between Cancari and Liplje. Then we have case which is protocol ID 1041/07 between Kravica and Zeleni Jadar 2. That one was illogical or not that illogical. At that time it was the problem with this one was that we did not have enough information regarding the specific location, as well as for the next one, Krke, Zeleni Jadar. I know that Krke is surface remains, and I'm not presenting in my chart these surface remains connections, but we have connection here. And the last one which is illogical is the last one on the next page, which is between Ravnice. Can you see it? Yes, indeed. It is Ravnice and Hodzici 5. And for all of these cases I have reviewed, because they were not logical to me, the autopsy reports and photographs from the exhumations. So I found in several instances, for example, that the entire body was found in one of those locations and then it was connected to body parts which were found in different locations. For example, Ravnice 2 and Hodzici 5, I think this is the case that we have the entire body in Hodzici 5 and parts of the bodies in Ravnice 2. I think this is the case, but I can't be sure. But I think that I've seen those cases, or you could see that for these illogical connections you can find the same part of the bodies in two -- in two places.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what did you do, if anything, to obtain clarification beyond looking at the autopsy reports?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. We have sent the -- our findings to the ICMP in order to get the clarification from their side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, if we could just go back one page in this exhibit, please. And you were mentioning a connection that is, I believe, 11 rows down. It's protocol number 1417/07 relating to or showing a reassociation between the site Kravica and the site Zeleni Jadar. Can you tell us a little bit more about what you know about this particular connection?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. When I was writing this report, I was not aware of the exact meaning of this case ID which is KA01-110-BP [Realtime transcript read in error KA01-00-BP] so I was not able to conclude anything. But just recently I have been reviewing the -- Michael Hedley's report. He was the crime of scene officer at the Kravica warehouse and he found the tooth of one individual, and you can find it in his report, and that he marked that tooth with exactly the same case ID as you can see it here, KA01-110-BP [Realtime transcript read in error KA01-00-BP]. So that was on 13 of October, 2000. And based on that we can conclude that we have DNA connection now between Kravica execution point and secondary mass grave Zeleni Jadar 2. That same individual or body parts of the same individual can be found also in Zeleni Jadar 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. For the record, because the reference is reported wrongly twice, the reference that the witness referred to was KA01-110-BP and not what appears on line 8 and line 13 of page 82. Thank you. Any time, Ms. Soljan. It's 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can stop now. I will have to continue briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We are going to stop here. I take it there is nothing changing in relation to Professor Parsons. Nothing. So tomorrow we're sitting in the afternoon. Thank you.
